steps.title: Understand
steps.text: A value is a piece of data. A variable gives it a name so you can use it later. Python treats text (str), whole numbers (int), decimal numbers (float), and truth values (bool) differently. Read these lines from the example: input() always returns text; int() and float() convert numeric text before calculation. The .2f format displays two decimal places.

steps.title: Predict
steps.text: Imagine the original example receives Ada Lovelace, 17, and 3.5, on separate lines. Make a prediction before revealing the explanation.

steps.title: Run
steps.text: Open the example and explicitly load the prepared inputs. Each line supplies one input() call; this is not an interactive terminal. Compare the Adult line in the console with your prediction. If you edited the example, its output may differ from the reference.

steps.title: Modify
steps.text: Try an age of 18 and a GPA of 3.567. Before running, predict whether Adult changes and how many decimal places GPA will show. You can edit the existing code or inputs; nothing is replaced automatically. Compare your prediction with the console output.

steps.title: Solve
steps.text: Exercise 01: read a positive count and summarize that many numbers. Exercise 02: split a product record and calculate price times quantity. Try your own approach, use a hint when stuck, then check each exercise. Checking uses the existing daily execution quota.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Check your understanding without running code. These questions do not approve programming exercises or use execution quota.

referenceOutput:
Name: Ada Lovelace
Age: 17
GPA: 3.50
Adult: False

prediction.prompt: What will the Adult line show for age 17?
prediction.explanation: age >= 18 compares two numbers and produces a bool. Seventeen is less than eighteen, so the result is False.

review.prompt: What type does input() return when you enter 17?
review.explanation: input() returns the text "17". int() converts that text to the number 17 when you need numeric comparisons or calculations.
"Ada" is not a whole-number representation. int("Ada") raises ValueError. Check whether the text is numeric or handle that exception.

review.prompt: Why check that the count is positive before calculating the average?

options.text: To avoid division by zero and an empty collection with no minimum or maximum.
Because Python cannot add decimal numbers.

review.explanation: With no values there is no minimum or maximum, and dividing the total by zero is invalid. Reject non-positive counts before reading values and calculating.

feedback.expectation: Read exactly N values and report their sum, average, minimum, and maximum.
feedback.suggestion: Check that the total includes every value and the average divides by the count.

feedback.expectation: Reject non-positive counts before calculating a summary.
feedback.suggestion: Check the guard before division, min(), or max().

feedback.caseName: edge: repeated values where minimum equals maximum
feedback.expectation: Repeated values must produce equal minimum and maximum.
feedback.suggestion: Check how minimum and maximum are initialized and updated.

feedback.expectation: Split the record into product, price, and quantity; report price times quantity.
feedback.suggestion: Check token order and numeric conversion before multiplication.

feedback.expectation: Reject a record with a missing field.
feedback.suggestion: Check the token count before unpacking the record.

feedback.expectation: A quantity of zero is valid and produces a total price of zero.
feedback.suggestion: Check whether a guard accidentally rejects zero quantity.

feedback.expectation: Reject extra fields instead of ignoring them.
feedback.suggestion: Check for exactly three tokens before conversion.
